articleTitle: Improved Q-Learning Control for Optimal Tracking of Underwater Vehicle Manipulator System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In this work, an improved Q learning control algorithm base on an extended state observer (ESO) is designed for an underwater vehicle manipulator system (UVMS). The UVMS is modeled as a nonlinear system with model uncertainties and external disturbances. In this paper, extended state observer (ESO) is constructed to evaluate the model uncertainties and external disturbances. In addition, an augmented system is constructed based on UVMS and reference signal. Furthermore, an improved Q learning control method is proposed to solve online the augmented algebraic Riccati equation (ARE) in the absence of the knowledge of the augmented system parameters. Finally, extensive numerical simulation results show that the effectiveness of the proposed optimal tracking control method for UVMS.

articleTitle: An Oversampling Method Based on KL-Divergence for Imbalanced Datasets and Credit Risk Assessment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Despite more than three decades of vigorous development, imbalanced learning is still attracted growing attention from both academic and finance. Skewed distributions for imbalanced datasets make classifiers biased towards the majority group. However, the opposite, the minority group, is more valuable in real world datasets. In this paper, we proposed an oversampling method E-SMOTE based on entropy theory to synthesis minority samples with designed weight over minority dangerous set. Firstly, positive dangerous samples are collected adaptively based on a division, where each minority sample is recognized as inner, danger or noise according to the distribution information of the nearest neighbors. Secondly, a sampling weight is designed based on KL-divergence of two distributions for one positive dangerous sample leaving or not. In other words, the sampling weight quantifies the importance of the positive dangerous sample. Finally, SMOTE synthesizes minority samples between positive dangerous sample and its nearest minority neighbors. In experiments, the proposed method is applied on 16 benchmark imbalanced datasets and the risk assessment problem of personal credit loan.

articleTitle: Application of Improved Rapid Spot Center Detection Algorithm in Spot Alignment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In order to achieve rapid laser spot alignment for laser communication, this paper proposes a laser spot center algorithm that combines coarse positioning and fine aiming, based on the concept of segmented control. The algorithm optimizes the image filtering process by analyzing the actual characteristics of the laser spot, considering the requirements of fast scanning speed and aiming accuracy. Adaptive median filtering and adaptive threshold segmentation are utilized to obtain a laser spot image with a uniform brightness distribution. The algorithm is theoretically and experimentally demonstrated to perform scanning and aiming tasks effectively under ideal conditions. Experimental results indicate that the proposed algorithm improves scanning speed by approximately 38.5% and aiming accuracy by about 28.6% compared to centroid methods and circle fitting algorithms. This image processing method can be employed to establish laser communication links between terminals.

articleTitle: A Power Method to Convex-Concave Minmax Optimization Problems with Nonlinear Constraints
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In this paper, we presents a new power penalty method to convex-concave minimax optimization problems with nonlinear constraints. This method first reformulate the KKT conditions of such optimization problem approximated by a nonlinear equation containing a power penalty term. Then we will show that the solution of the penalty equation converges to that of the mixed complementarity problem at an exponential rate, which is depending on the parameters in the penalty equation, and some numerical results are presented to verify the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Endpoint Control of Manipulator Driven by Dual Neurodynamic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In this paper, the time-varying neurodynamic algorithm is explained as a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) with inputs. A collaborative computational method for neurodynamic algorithms is proposed via connecting neural networks by time-varying parameters as input of network and this method is used to compute a control strategy for the endpoint of the manipulator. The motion of the endpoint of the manipulator is planned through an optimization problem and solved using a neurodynamic algorithm. The state output of this neurodynamic algorithm is mapped to a distributed motor set at each joint through an optimal joint angular velocity programming problem. This distributed motor set assigns the required angular velocity of the joints to each motor through an allocation problem and the corresponding neurodynamic algorithm. The control of the entire manipulator is achieved through the cooperative use of two neural network. Benefiting from the time varying neurodynamic algorithm being a method with continuous dynamical behaviour and being able to respond to time varying inputs, the proposed multiple neurodynamic algorithms collaborative approach is a parallel computational method that can be implemented in hardware. Numerical simulation experiments were conducted to achieve endpoint control of a manipulator using dual neurodynamic algorithms.

articleTitle: A Peephole Bidirectional the Long Short-Term Memory Network for Multi-Scale Imbalanced Time Series Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: For unbalanced multivariate time series with missing values, a multi-scale prediction model based on long short-term memory network variant (multi-PB-LSTM) is constructed. The multi-PB-LSTM utilizes multi-task Gaussian processes to transform asynchronous time series into unified and complete input data by learning the correlation between timestamps and features. At the same time, several classifiers based on LSTM variants are constructed aiming to capture dependencies over a long span in sequence data. Finally, through the decision fusion component of the multi-PB-LSTM model, the prediction results of each classifier are combined to obtain the final classification result. The proposed model can achieve satisfactory performance on some public datasets (MIMIC-III, PhysioNet).

articleTitle: Research on Big Data Mining and Application Based on Roll Up and Drill Down Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: To improve the efficiency of big data mining while ensuring the accuracy of mining results. Propose a big data mining method based on roll up and drill down techniques. By using roll up techniques to achieve feature aggregation, reduce the number of features, improve time efficiency, and analyze the mining results to determine the target clustering features. Drill down on the target clustering features to ensure the accuracy of the mining results. The experiment uses the independently created Mongolian medicine formula datasets as a case study to provide specific applications. The experimental results show that the time efficiency and efficiency improvement rate of mining result generation have been improved to a certain extent under various expansion data multiples, and the three error rate indicators of mining results have also been improved. Therefore, this method can not only improve the efficiency of big data mining, but also ensure the accuracy of mining results.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Water Flow Optimizer Incorporating Adaptive Weights and Search Step Sizes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Meta-heuristic algorithms are highly regarded for their exceptional global search capability. In recent years, a novel natural inspired algorithm known as the Water Flow Optimizer (WFO) has emerged. This algorithm mimics the laminar and turbulent flow phenomena observed in natural water systems and showcases remarkable optimization performance. However, similar to other meta-heuristic algorithms, WFO still suffers from the drawback of getting trapped in local optima. In this paper, we propose an enhanced water flow optimizer (AWS-WFO) based on adaptive weights and search step sizes to prevent the algorithm from getting stuck in local optima. AWS-WFO considers the weights and adaptive exploration performance mechanism, draws inspiration from the advantageous features of LDIWPSO (Linearly Decreasing Inertia Weight Particle Swarm Optimization) and effectively enhances the optimization performance of WFO. In order to evaluate the performance of the proposed AWS-WFO algorithm, comparative experiments were conducted using seven widely recognized test functions as benchmarks. The experimental results indicate that the proposed algorithm exhibits a certain level of competitiveness.

Author Keywords: adaptive weights and search step sizes

articleTitle: SAM-GAN: A Single-Image GAN Model Guided by Synergistic Attention
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In real life, there is often an insufficient number of images available for the model to learn from in image generation tasks. Previous work shows that learning the distribution of patches within a single image can possibly gain powerful prior. But training a single-image generative model is still a tough mission since the features of an image patch are considerably less detailed and abstract compared to a distribution of images. That's why the existing methods are relatively rare, such as SinGAN, ConSinGAN, and CCASinGAN. This paper proposes a single-image GAN model (SAM-GAN) guided by a synergistic attention mechanism which consists of low-dimensional and high-dimensional blocks focusing on both global structural and detailed texture features in the meantime. We conduct numerous experiments to evaluate the model's performance qualitatively and quantitatively. The outcomes demonstrate SAM-GAN's superiority over other state-of-the-art models, showcasing its potential to generate more intricate and realistic images.

articleTitle: Target Guided Knowledge Distillation for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Existing few-shot classification methods will suffer severe performance degradation when there is a domain gap between the base classes data used for training and the new classes data used for the downstream task. For this reason, cross-domain few-shot learning (CD-FSL) is trying to solve this problem that exists in few-shot learning (FSL), which breaks the restrictive hypothesis that the base (source) classes and the novel (target) classes are sampled from the same domain in FSL. Due to the domain gap between the source and target domain data, the model trained on the source domain often has a deviation when transferred to the target domain, which leads to the model not being well generalized to the target task and produces the problem of inadaptation. To overcome this problem, a new target guided knowledge distillation (TGKD) framework is proposed in this work. We design two distinct knowledge distillation methods to enhance the generalization of the model and its pertinence to the target task in the teacher training and knowledge distillation stages, respectively. Specifically, in the teacher training phase, we propose a self-cross distillation to reduce intra-class semantic variations, thereby improving the robustness of the model's feature representation. In the knowledge distillation phase, a dual-student network is proposed to alleviate the bias of the model when migrating to the target data by utilizing a small portion of unlabeled target samples. Extensive experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: A Two-Tiered Destructive Iterated Greedy Approach for Enhancing Efficiency in Multi-Factory Hybrid Flow Shop Scheduling with Blocking Constraint
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In the context of economic globalization, distributed manufacturing models are gradually emerging in large enterprises in order to provide faster demand response. In this paper, we study the distributed hybrid flow shop scheduling problem with blocking constraints (DBHFSP), whose optimization objective is makespan. A two-tiered destructive iterated greedy (tIG) algorithm is developed to optimize DBHFSP. First, the NEH2 heuristic is used to generate the initial solution; second, a cross-factory neighborhood structure is designed to coordinate the global search capability of the algorithm; to further explore the neighborhood space of the solution, we propose a permutation-based local strengthening strategy; finally, the simulated annealing (SA) method is used to augment the diversity of the algorithm. We conduct simulation experiments on 60 instances, and the experimental results prove that tIG outperforms other comparison algorithms.

articleTitle: Adaptive Multilayer Method of Fundamental Solutions for the Scattering Problem of an Interior Cavity
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In this paper, the direct scattering problem of an interior cavity is considered. And the adaptive multilayer method of fundamental solutions (MFS) is used to solve it. The source points are placed on multilayer artificial boundaries, and an adaptive weighted greedy algorithm is introduced to select the significant source points. Compared with the traditional MFS, the number of source points required in the multilayer MFS is reduced for the same accuracy. With the same number of source points, the accuracy of the multilayer MFS is higher than the traditional MFS. In order to verify the effectiveness of multilayer MFS, some computational examples are given.

articleTitle: Application of ResLSTM in Hypomimia Video Detection for Parkinson's Disease
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Hypomimia is one of the primary clinical manifestations of Parkinson's disease, characterized by a reduction in facial expressions and progressive loss of facial animation. In routine clinical diagnosis, the assessment of Hypomimia remains subjective and relies on manual scoring by doctors. With the development of artificial intelligence, digital healthcare has become an essential component of the medical ecosystem. In this paper, we explore a method for diagnosing Parkinson's disease Hypomimia symptoms by analyzing facial videos using deep learning. We collected facial expression videos from PD patients and matched control groups from open-source resources. After preprocessing the video frames, we employed deep learning algorithms to diagnose Hypomimia. Experimental results show that our model achieved an average accuracy of 81.73% in the Hypomimia classification task. This research contributes to the digitized diagnosis of Parkinson's disease based on facial videos and validates our PD Hypomimia diagnostic model through experiments. The research findings in this paper have potential applications in assisting with preliminary home-based symptom assessment.

articleTitle: Logging Lithology Identification of Unconventional Reservoir Based on Hybrid Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Lithology identification is an important foundation for comprehensive evaluation of shale reservoir logging. Shale reservoirs have complex and significant heterogeneity, it is of great significance to effectively recognize their lithology. However, under complex geological conditions, the relationship between logging response and lithology is weak, and lithology identification relies on the geological experience of logging interpreters; The cost of lithology data is high, sampling is difficult, and accurate characterization of lithology is difficult in the case of lack of sample size. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a lithology identification method based on the combination of convolutional neural network (CNN) and support vector machine (SVM). On the one hand, the feature information between logging data and lithology is automatically extracted by CNN, and on the other hand, SVM is utilized to solve the problem of small sample size. Using seven conventional logging curves such as spontaneous potential (SP) and deep, shallow lateral resistivity (RD, RS) as training data. The results show that compared with CNN and SVM, the performance of the hybrid model is more robust. The recognition accuracy of well H2 reaches 91.95%, which confirms the higher recognition accuracy and generalization ability of the new method.

articleTitle: A Modified Learning Method for First-order Takagi-Sugeno Fuzzy System: Gradient-based Neuro-fuzzy Algorithm Employing Smoothing Group Lasso Regularization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: The first-order Takagi-Sugeno (TS1) fuzzy system harbors an assemblage of IF-THEN fuzzy rules and is capable of approximating nonlinear systems of arbitrary complexity via discerning suitable affiliation functions and rules. As a natural extension of the lasso, group lasso adeptly trims superfluous connections among neurons and disposes the variable selection issue at the group stratum. Nonetheless, a fundamental shortcomings arises when the group lasso regularizer is directly applied during network training, particularly evident as weights converge towards zero, that is numerical oscillations. In addressing this concern, a smoothing function is introduced to approximate the original group lasso regularization (OGLR). Building upon the aforementioned content, a novel gradient-based neuro-fuzzy learning algorithm with smoothing group lasso regularization (SGLR) for the TS1 fuzzy system is proposed. Ultimately, the efficacy of the proposed algorithm is substantiated through three simulations that validate its sparse performance, approximation capability, and generalization potential.

articleTitle: Image Dehazing Method Based on Enhancement and Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Due to incomplete dehazing, low contrast, and poor visibility in traditional image dehazing algorithms, we propose a dehazing method that combines several image enhancement approaches. The adaptive Gamma correction is utilized to improve the clarity of the hazy image, and the adaptive histogram equalization method with limited contrast is used to enhance the contrast and brightness. Then, the dehazed image is obtained by the multi-exposure fusion method. The experimental results show that the proposed method has better clarity and brightness on the dehazed image. Compared with the classical image dehazing algorithm, this method not only can retain more detailed information, but also the dehazed images are more natural, and dehazing effect is remarkable.

articleTitle: Variable Sample-Size Forward-Backward-Forward Algorithm for Two-Stage Stochastic Variational Inequality
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In this paper, paper, we propose a novel approach called the variable sample-size forward-backward-forward algorithm to address the two-stage stochastic variational inequality. A key advantage of our algorithm is its requirement for only one projection onto the closed convex set per iteration. By making reasonable assumptions, we demonstrate that the sequence generated by our algorithm converges almost surely. Furthermore, we establish a linear convergence rate for the difference between iterates and solutions, thereby achieving efficient convergence. To validate our proposed method, numerical experiments are conducted to showcase its effectiveness.

articleTitle: An Efficient Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Neural Network Based Classifier
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In this paper, a simplified Karnik-Mendel (SKM) is proposed to realize type reduction for type-2 fuzzy models. To construct the fuzzy rule based neural network classifier, the clustering algorithm is employed to generate the nodes in the network, and we explain the interpretable construction process detailedly. In addition, to improve the classification performance, a long term memory based gradient optimization strategy is presented to optimize the structure parameters. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed model EIT2FNN-C is verified by 2 benchmark classification data sets.

articleTitle: A Multi-Strategy Improved Butterfly Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Butterfly optimization algorithm (BOA) is an excellent swarm intelligence algorithm that simulates the foraging behavior of butterfly populations, but it has such defects as poor accuracy, easy to stagnate at the local optimum, insufficient convergence and no balance between exploitation and exploration. Hence this paper proposes a multi-strategy improved butterfly optimization algorithm (MIBOA). By introducing four optimization strategies, including Bernoulli chaos map, dynamic switch probability, adaptive inertia weight and opposite-based learning, the above problems are effectively improved. And MIBOA is compared with other swarm intelligence algorithms on eight classical benchmark functions. The results demonstrate its excellent optimization performance and robustness.

articleTitle: Explainable Prediction Model of Logging Lithology Classification Based on XGBoost and SHAP
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Lithology identification is a key and difficult problem in geological interpretation of reservoirs. To accurately predict the rock types in the target area of oil and gas exploration and provide correct reservoir lithology, an explainable model of lithology classification combining XGBoost and SHAP has been proposed. The model can achieve both good classification and explanation ability. Firstly, the lithologic classification model is established by the limit gradient lifting (XGBoost) algorithm, and the K-fold cross-validation (K-fold CV) and grid search algorithm are used to find the optimal hyperparameter combination of the model. Then, the predicted value of the optimized XGBoost model is compared with the random forest algorithm and support vector machine algorithm by using different evaluation indexes, and the overall and local explanation of the predicted result of the XGBoost model is given by using the SHAP method. The experimental results show that the lithologic identification model established by the XGBoost method optimized by hyperparameter adjustment has achieved good effects in the actual data test, and the SHAP method can effectively explain the output of the XGBoost model.

articleTitle: Hybrid Control on Stability and Bifurcation for a Delayed Complex Networks Fractional-Order Model of Disease Spreading
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: This paper explores the Hopf bifurcation behavior of a general nonlinear disease spreading model with hybrid control. When hybrid control is applied to the system, the stability of the system can be significantly improved by adjusting the controller parameter. Firstly, the characteristic equation is circumspectly researched by choosing time delay as the bifurcation parameter, and the criteria is derived for the stability and Hopf bifurcation of the system under hybrid control. Then the bifurcation diagram and stable area of the system is obtained through numerical simulation. We also found that link-adding probability, fractional order and nonlinear interaction coefficient can also effectively influence the dynamic behavior of such networks. And with the decrease of these system parameters, the stability of the system is improved. Finally, the validity of the conclusion was verified through sensitivity analysis.

articleTitle: An Improved Iterative Reduction FISTA-Barzilai-Borwein Algorithm for Large-Scale LASSO
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: The iterative reduction FISTA algorithm (IR-FISTA-B) is an extremely excellent algorithm for solving large-scale LASSO problems. It utilizes the sparsity and gradient of the solution to transform large-scale problems into small-scale subproblems, and uses the FISTA algorithm to solve subproblems. In this paper, we improve the algorithm by using the Barzilai-Borwein step size as the step factor in the inner loop algorithm, and provide appropriate parameter update criteria to accelerate the convergence rate of the algorithm. Under the ideal termination criterion, we prove that the algorithm converges to a minimum with a locally linear rate. In numerical experiments, the performance of the proposed algorithm for solving large-scale LASSO problems was demonstrated by testing on synthetic data and LIBSVM datasets comparing with the original algorithm.

articleTitle: Group Regularization Learning with Dynamic Regularization Factor Based on BN Layer Scaling Factor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Convolutional neural network (CNN) is increasingly known as computation-intensive and memory-intensive models, which hinder their deployment on embedded systems. Attempts have been made to compress CNNs using the pruning method, especially structured pruning, which can achieve a compact network without affecting the original accuracy. Group regularization methods are usually used to achieve structured pruning. However, existing group regularization methods usually use a fixed regularization factor to compress weights towards zero, which has an unreasonable presupposition that all weights are equally important. To solve this issue, we propose a group regularization with dynamic regularization factor by combining regularization-based structured pruning and importance-based structured pruning, named DRFGR. It assigns a different and updatable regularization factor for each filter based on the scaling factors of the Batch Normalization (BN) layer, which represents the importance of the filters. The efficiency of DRFGR has been verified by empirical analysis on the CIFAR10 dataset with popular CNNs. The results show that DRFGR can compress the network more adequately than the method with a fixed regularization factor, while also improving accuracy.

articleTitle: A UI Layout Generation Method Based on Shared Feature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: The generative model that can produce different UI layouts based on text input is a valuable tool for assisting UI design. It can significantly reduce the time and cost of manually designing UI interfaces and is also an important task in cross-modal generation, such as text-to-image conversion. We first use an object detection network to capture layout information in the interface and generate constrained text from images. At the same time, we share the features learned in the intermediate process with the interface generation network to enhance the consistency between constrained text and the final interface. Then, we use a two-stage Stack GAN to convert constrained text into UI layouts. The encoder in the GAN network directly uses the feature extraction layer from the object detection network, saving training time and sharing feature extraction from images. Our proposed shared feature extraction method, compared to a network that does not share features, can improve content consistency by approximately 14% without changing network complexity and depth. Finally, on the Rico dataset, we achieved an average IS of 4.36, an average FID of 28.26, and an average R precision of 89.82%.

articleTitle: YOLOv7-CBAM for Similar Casting Inspection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: The process of classifying industrial castings and putting them into boxes heavily relies on human vision for judgment. When castings share similar colors, shapes, and sizes, manual classification often leads to misjudgments and inefficiencies, significantly impacting economic outcomes and product reputation. Consequently, rapid, accurate, and automated inspection and identification of industrial castings have become pivotal tasks. This study focuses on the arc-shaped pipe castings primarily used in firefighting applications. Leveraging the distinguishing feature of varying identification strings on similar castings, the research employs object detection techniques from computer vision. It integrates cameras for inspection and recognition, thereby considerably reducing costs and enhancing product efficiency. The main research work is to integrate the spatial and channel attention module (CBAM), which can improve the representation and differentiation of features, into the YOLOv7 framework, to better focus on feature information, capable of enhancing feature representation and discriminability. Moreover, to enhance the generalization and robustness of the model, data enhancement is carried out. At the same time, to strengthen the feature differentiation, the study innovatively introduces a dual-label annotation approach tailored to cases where similar castings only differ in identification strings. Comparative experiments demonstrate that CBAM-enhanced YOLOv7 achieves a MAP@0.5 of 99.91%, with a frames-per-second (FPS) rate of 33.41, it fully meets the requirements of accuracy and speed of casting inspection. Exceptional on-site performance of the model in factory tests validates the proposed method's effectiveness, offering valuable insights and strategies for addressing analogous challenges in industrial environments.

articleTitle: Mechanistic and Data-Driven Modelling of Operational Parameters Prediction on Oil and Gas Transportation Pipeline Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Collection and transportation pipeline network of Crude oil is one of the critical infrastructures in a largescale oilfield. Fewer sensors are installed in the pipeline network and the collection is not timely, which makes it difficult to control the transportation of crude oil in the pipeline network in real time. Due to the lack of standards for data collection, traditional data-driven methods are difficult to achieve expected results. Therefore, a dual-driven modeling method of both mechanism and data is proposed to realize the integrated prediction of operating parameters at each place of the pipeline network. The real-time production data from each wellhead are input into the model. The pressure and temperature at each place of the pipeline are calculated by the Beggs-Bril and Leapienzon equations. The measured and calculated values are input into the transformer-based model with the constraints of storage and transportation mechanism. The calculated results of the equations are corrected for errors to achieve the purpose of accuracy. Results from experiments in oilfield gathering and transportation pipeline networks show that our model has the best prediction accuracy and generalization ability. Through a detailed ablation study, we demonstrate the effectiveness of each contribution in the overall architecture and methodology. The results show that the mechanism and data modeling approach outperform the storage and transportation mechanism model and the purely data-driven model.

articleTitle: Application of Random Forest Algorithm with Bayesian Optimization to Reservoir Prediction: Application of Random Forest Algorithm with Bayesian Optimization to Reservoir Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Reservoir prediction in the actual work area is usually based on the characteristics of logging data, combined with the experience of experts in the work area to carry out manual judgment, which is not only time-consuming but also has a strong subjective factor. The parameter information of conventional logging data is enough, but when reservoir prediction is extended to three-dimensional seismic data, only elastic parameters can be used. Therefore, it is particularly important to predict reservoirs based on a limited number of elastic parameters. The random forest algorithm has achieved good results in reservoir prediction of well logging data. How to extend the random forest algorithm to seismic data for reservoir prediction, improve its performance, and avoid the phenomenon of local optimal solutions in the algorithm is still a problem that needs to be solved. In this paper, we construct a variety of sensitive parameters from elastic parameters such as longitudinal wave velocity, transverse wave velocity and longitudinal and transverse wave velocity ratio, and establish a set of reservoir prediction method flow with Bayesian optimization of Random Forest. For the sample imbalance problem in the training samples, adaptive sample weighting is introduced to improve the attention to the less class samples, and the results show that the method is more accurate than the traditional random forest in reservoir prediction on the logging-seismic scale. The final reservoir prediction accuracy on seismic scale reaches 86.4%.

articleTitle: MFAM-Net:A Surface Defect Detection Network for Strip Steel via Multiscale Feature Fusion and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Detecting defects on the surface of steel strip is a critical step in the production field of the steel industry. However, due to the diversity of defect types, scales, texture structures and the irregular distribution of defects in strip steel images, existing detection methods are difficult to achieve accurate detection. To this end, we propose a steel strip surface defect detection network (MFAM-Net) based on an YOLOv5 model. Firstly, we design a multi-scale feature extraction module (MSC3) to capture more complete and comprehensive defect texture features for strip defect objects with large scale changes. Secondly, we add the coordinate attention module (CA) to the network, while the spatial pyramid pooling structure (SPPF) of the backbone network is also replaced to increase the network's ability to locate defect features. Third, we introduce a new detection branch to improve the network's detection performance for faults of various sizes. Finally, we introduce the Wise-IoU (WIoU) loss function to focus the detection network on ordinary quality anchor boxes, and enhance the network's regression capability for defect positions. Experimental results show that on the NEU-DET and GC10-DET datasets, our method achieves an mean average precision of 83.5% and 66.7%, respectively, which is 7% and 2.9% higher than the baseline network YOLOv5, and also outperforms other defect detection models.

articleTitle: Glaucoma Fundus Image Recognition Based on Optimal ROI Proportion and VIT-B/16
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In order to improve the training efficiency of deep neural network models in glaucoma fundus image recognition tasks, this paper proposes a fundus image data processing method of the optimal proportion of Region of Interest (ROI). Firstly, the glaucoma fundus images and normal fundus images in the OIA-ODIR dataset were organized, and the resulting dataset was preprocessed with data augmentation which is only applied on negative sample data and histogram homogenization. Secondly, the preprocessed data was extracted separately with different ROI proportions centered around the optic disc and cup. Then datasets with different ROI proportions are used to train the VIT-B/16 model separately, and the optimal proportion of ROI makes it has the highest ratio of accuracy to training time. The experimental results showed that the optimal ROI proportion was 20%. Finally, the same data augmentation was performed on the dataset with the optimal ROI proportion and the original proportion separately. The results of training VIT -B/16 on these two kinds of dataset showed that using the optimal ROI ratio to process the data can reduce the training time of the VIT-B/16 model on the OIA-ODIR fundus dataset by 80.15%. The data processing method proposed in this article can effectively reduce the dependence of model training on hardware.

articleTitle: Highway Debris Detection Algorithm Based on Vehicle Trajectories
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Highway debris is one of the main causes of highway accidents, so detecting highway debris is an important task for road safety. However, the problem is challenging because it involves a large number of factors, including the speed and direction of the vehicle, the condition of the roadway, and the type and location of the debris. In this paper, we propose a highway debris detection algorithm based on vehicle trajectories that combines deep learning and traditional methods. The algorithm segments the detection process into multiple modules. Firstly, the initialization module acquires video stream information and performs region of interest (ROI) labeling. Subsequently, the detection-tracking module is employed to detect and track high-speed vehicle targets in real-time. In the debris judgment module, two core algorithms are used: curvature-based judgment of sharp turns and lane change judgment based on linear fitting. These algorithms analyze the trajectory of the vehicle to infer the potential presence of debris. Finally, the alarm is triggered by the alarm message generation module to complete the detection of highway debris on the whole highway. After testing the actual road monitoring video, the algorithm is able to accurately determine the highway debris and make accurate identification and alarm, with the advantages of real-time, high efficiency and accuracy.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Based Active Disturbance Rejection Control for Underwater Vehicle Manipulator System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of trajectory tracking control for the underwater vehicle manipulator system (UVMS) with parameter uncertainty and external disturbances. An adaptive linear active disturbance rejection control (ALADRC) scheme is proposed by combining ADRC and model-free adaptive control. Firstly, the UVMS dynamics model is discretized and converted into an equivalent dynamic linearization data model. Secondly, a parameter estimation law and an adaptive extended state observer are designed to estimate the pseudo-partial derivative matrix and the total disturbance in the data model respectively. Then, an adaptive LADRC law is designed to compensate the total disturbance to realize the trajectory tracking control. The proposed ALADRC is a typical data-driven solution, which only requires input-output data to achieve effective performance. Furthermore, the stability analysis of the designed control system is given. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme is verified by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Anti-Occlusion UAV Target Detection Based on Attention Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: UAVs have developed rapidly in recent years, and their scope of application has been expanding. However, it has also given rise to various problems, such as illegal surveying and mapping and flights in no-fly zones. In order to quickly detect UAV targets during these events and take appropriate measures, it has become particularly important to study UAV target detection. For UAV images captured in real scenarios, there is object occlusion and background blending in UAV images. This makes it difficult to detect UAVs hidden in their surroundings. Therefore to solve the problem that UAVs are difficult to detect, an improved UAV detection algorithm YOLOv7_AUTD (Anti-occlusion UAV Target Detection) is proposed based on YOLOv7. The improvement includes: firstly, FPN network integration with the CSP module, ensuring lightweight while obtaining gradient flow information; secondly, adding CA attention mechanism, while introducing channel attention mechanism, taking into account spatial attention mechanism; finally, the Focal loss function is used to solve the problem of imbalanced proportion of positive and negative samples, and the E-iou function is used for more accurate boundary box regression to improve the accuracy of localization. The experimental results show that compared with the YOLO7 algorithm, the proposed algorithm improves AP by 2.72%.

articleTitle: A Heuristic Repelling Strategy for Accelerating the Global Convergence of Intelligent Optimization Algorithms - A Case Study on Differential Evolution Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: This work proposed a heuristic-based strategy to improve the global convergence of Intelligent Optimization Al-gorithms (IOAs) by scrutinizing their evolutionary mechanisms. Specifically, according to Gaussian and Cauchy distribution functions, six potential individuals were generated primarily based on the current best, worst, and farthest one from the best in the population. Then, they replaced the six least effective individuals, and the rest remained unchanged to form a new population to continue evolving. This process was repeated until termination. A case study on the Differential Evolution (DE) algorithm was detailed. Simulations on 21 benchmark functions, including 13 high-dimensional ones, demonstrated improved accuracy and reduced computational effort compared to some existing methods. The parameter settings also became more lenient, and the strategy showed potential for applicability to other swarm intelligence-like algorithms.

articleTitle: Phase Retrieval Based RIDNet Denoising Algorithm for Color Image
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: The phase retrieval problem refers to recovering the original signal from only amplitude measurements. The detector CCD can only seek the intensity information in the diffraction field, and the phase is generally lost. The phase retrieval problem is non-linear, and it is difficult to reconstruct the original from only the amplitude of the color image. The phase retrieval algorithm, based on RIDNet denoising(RIDNetPR) is proposed to deal with color image reconstruction. First, the features are extracted using RIDNet, and multiple Enhancement Attention Modules (EAM) are repeatedly stacked for color image denoising tasks to ensure the ability of the deep learning network for feature extraction. Regularization terms constrain the network by improving the recovery accuracy. Second, the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) is utilized to reconstruct the original color images. Compared with traditional phase retrieval algorithms, the experimental results show that the proposed algorithm improves the Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and Structure Similarity Index Measure(SSIM) values at different Gaussian noise levels. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is illustrated for color image.

articleTitle: Ocean Wave Information Extraction from Raw Ocean Video Based on Self-Attention ConvLSTM
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Precise wave information is essential for assessing fatigue damage to offshore wind turbines. This study explores a visual method based on ConvLSTM combined with CNN and self-attention memory to extract ocean wave details. The network extracts both temporal and spatial information from wave impact videos to estimate significant wave height (Hs) and wave peak frequency (fp). Separate training for Hs and fp demonstrates the network's accuracy under varying imaging conditions. Additionally, the inclusion of a self-attention memory module based on ConvLSTM enhances model performance, improving prediction and regression capabilities.

articleTitle: ConvNeXt Block-Based Deep Learning Surrogate Model for Polymer-Flooding Reservoir Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Surrogate modeling has emerged as a crucial strategy for time and cost savings in reservoir development. However, the majority of research on surrogate modeling has been concentrated on secondary reservoir development processes such as water or gas flooding, with limited focus on surrogate modeling for tertiary oil recovery techniques like polymer flooding. In this paper, we emphasize the utilization of deep modeling techniques and introduce a deep encoder-decoder neural network to establish a high-dimensional nonlinear dynamic mapping surrogate model for uncertainty parameters associated with polymer flooding. Specifically, this model maps uncertain grid permeability parameters to reservoir state variables such as pressure, saturation, and polymer concentration. The model employs an encoder network to extract high-dimensional coarse features of input parameters, followed by a decoder network to refine these features to obtain the final model outputs. Experimental results from applying this model to the dynamic prediction of a two-dimensional synthetic polymer flooding model show improved prediction accuracy compared to two existing surrogate models, while simultaneously reducing computational time for reservoir simulators, thus maintaining prediction precision.

articleTitle: Research on Oversampling Method of Imbalanced Dataset Based on Improved Generative Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Binary classification frequently entails the challenge of imbalanced datasets, characterized by substantial disparities in sample sizes between the two different classes. The data imbalance usually makes it difficult for classifiers to learn positive samples, leading to unsatisfactory classification effects. Generative adversarial network (GAN) can be used as an oversampling method to rectify data imbalance by generating positive samples. However, when confronted with a multi-cluster distribution of positive samples, GAN often experiences a mode collapse, that is, only a partial distribution of a few samples can be learned, resulting in the aggregation of generated data into a cluster or a segment. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a novel method MIX-NOISE GAN. It employs Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) to generate GMM noise that aligns with the distribution of positive samples. The GMM noise is then combined with traditional random noise as the generator input, referred to as the mixture of noise. Empirical results and visualizations from experiments conducted on simulated and benchmark datasets demonstrate that MIX-NOISE GAN significantly enhances classification performance on 17 imbalanced datasets compared to six classical sampling methods in terms of G-mean, F-measure, and AVC.

articleTitle: Prediction of Multiphase Flow in Fractured Porous Media Using Physics-Informed Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Prediction of multiphase flow in fractured porous media is important to lots of engineering practices. In this work, we present a Physics-Informed Convolutional Neural Network (PICNN) for solving multiphase flow in fractured porous media. Specifically, the Embedded Discrete Fracture Model (EDFM) is adopted to explicitly represent fractures, the PDE residual in loss function is constructed via the Finite Volume Method (FVM) such that the flux continuity between neighboring cells of different properties (e.g. matrix and fracture) is defined rigorously, and then we apply the Implicit-Pressure Explicit-Saturation (IMPES) scheme to calculate pressure and saturation, in which only a single CNN needs to be trained per time step. Finally, we demonstrate the accuracy and application of the proposed approach to capture the impact of fractures on multiphase flow in fractured porous media.

articleTitle: Music Transcription Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Automatic Music Transcription (AMT), facilitating music composition, editing, and performance, aims at transcribing music to scores that can be read and modified. It also plays a part in enhancing efficiency in music work, music education, and protecting music copyrights. In this paper, we reviewed two deep learning-based AMT models: MT3 based on T5 transformer, and DiffRoll based on diffusion model. We also analyzed the performance of the two models on different music datasets like MAESTRO and MAPS and explored their unique features.

articleTitle: Solar Radio Spectrum Classification by Deep Conventional Neural Network Based on Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: The damage to communication facilities and navigation equipments may be caused by the violent solar radio explosion. With the emergence of high-performance observation equipments, solar data shows a tremendous growth trend. Deep learning, especially convolutional neural network, is used to classify solar radio spectrum images because it performs well in the processing of massive data, especially image data. In response to the lack of solar image datasets, a transfer learning method based on four pre-trained models with ImageNet image dataset is improved to solve the problem of classifying and recognizing three categories of solar spectral images. The experimental results show that MobileNet based on this model can achieve 98.95% accuracy, while the training speed of the model is improved also.

articleTitle: Utilizing the NEEP Model to Predict the Compressive Strength of Cement
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In the construction industry, cement is widely used, and its quality standards are particularly stringent. Among these standards, the compressive strength of cement is one of the most crucial quality indicators. However, existing measurement methods are time-consuming and resource-intensive. This study adopts an innovative symbolic regression methodology to swiftly evaluate cement's compressive strength for quality assessment, even prior to the initiation of the hydration process. Additionally, it facilitates parameter analysis to explore the impact of cement raw material ratios on compressive strength. Additionally, it allows for parameter analysis, enabling research into the impact of cement raw material ratios on compressive strength. Experimental results demonstrate that this algorithm accurately predicts strength and exhibits excellent generalization capabilities.

articleTitle: Some Thoughts on Constructing Domain Multi-Modal Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence, massive and multi-modal data continue to accumulate and precipitate. How to efficiently utilize rich data resources, efficiently manage massive information in an orderly way, realize multi-modal data convergence and fusion, and improve data enabling ability has become a key and challenging problem faced by all fields. As a means of new quality technology, knowledge graph is widely used in all walks of life, and its powerful intelligent search function is favored by people. However, there is still a lack of in-depth research on how to converge and integrate multi-modal data and break the semantic differences and heterogeneity among data. On the basis of the traditional knowledge graph, more and more experts focus their research on the multi-modal knowledge graph. Combined with the previous research work on the multi-modal knowledge graph, this paper considers how to construct the domain multi-modal knowledge graph on the basis of fully recognizing and understanding the multi-modal knowledge graph. It aims to accurately grasp the definition, value significance, construction mode and problems in the construction process of domain multi-modal knowledge graph.

articleTitle: AGraphDTA: An Efficient Model for Drug-Target Affinity Prediction with Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: It is a crucial task to predict the Drug-target affinity (DTA) in drug discovery. Recently, the application of deep learning shows a significant improvement on DTA prediction. However, most previous methods have struggled to extract the complex information of proteins. Hence, this paper introduces a novel model named AGraphDTA for DTA prediction. Specifically, AGraphDTA employs Graph Neural Network (GNN) to extract graph features of drugs and proteins. Then it employs Convo-lutional Neural Network (CNN) to extract amino acid sequence features. Additionally, a fusing block is employed to generate the fusion feature that represent the complex information of proteins. Evaluation results on benchmark datasets show that AGraphDTA demonstrates a superior performance in DTA prediction.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Improved Collaborative Filtering Algorithm in Course Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In the era of big data, the amount of resources on educational platforms is constantly increasing, making it difficult for many learners to choose the courses they really need from a massive number of online courses. Collaborative filtering algorithms are widely used in recommendation systems. Traditional collaborative filtering algorithms usually use the cosine similarity formula for interest similarity calculation, but in many cases, popular courses can affect the recommendation results and cannot reflect student needs well. This article proposes an improved solution to the cosine similarity calculation formula of traditional collaborative filtering algorithms, which can effectively suppress the influence of popular courses on the actual similarity of students. Experimental results show that this method can efficiently recommend online courses on educational platforms.

articleTitle: An Efficient Algorithm for a Locating Model of Marine Oil Spill
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Marine oil spill occurs frequently and seriously affects the balance of ocean ecology with continuous resource exploitation and utilization in the Bohai Sea. It damages the sustained economic and social development. This paper studies the oil spill accident of Penglai 19–3 oilfield in Bohai Bay. Through defining the oil film of marine oil spill as numerous oil particles, the oil particle coordinates can be obtained by isolated forest with decision tree algorithm. The number of oil spilling points can be determined by density clustering and fitted by Gaussian mixture clustering. We build a location model of marine oil spill based on clustering algorithm and can get the accurate location of oil spill in the ocean. The model can help us to accurately monitor the ocean oil leakage in real time, make timely response and reduce the loss caused by oil spill.

articleTitle: UOD-FPN: An Effective Feature Pyramid Network for Underwater Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Optical images captured in underwater environments often suffer from degradation problems such as color deviation, low contrast, and haze effects. Faced with this situation, traditional feature pyramid networks (FPNs) have difficulty effectively integrating the multi-scale features of underwater objects, which limits the performance of object detectors in underwater environments. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel underwater object detection feature pyramid network (UOD-FPN), which can effectively enhance the ability to represent underwater object features. This network consists of three different modules. First, the inter-layer feature fusion module (IFM) is capable of generating multiple aggregated feature layers with different receptive fields. Second, the feature adaptive weighted re-layering module (FAWRM) introduces attention mechanisms to guide finer re-layering of the aggregated feature layer. Finally, the feature-selective fusion module (FFM) achieves more effective feature fusion by using cross-correlation responses between different feature layers as guidance, enhancing the ability to express multi-level integrated features. Additionally, the UOD-FPN proposed in this paper can be applied to most FPN-based object detection models. The experiments demonstrate that UOD-FPN can significantly enhance the performance of one-stage and two-stage object detectors on the underwater datasets DUO and RUOD.

articleTitle: Asynchronous Control for T-S Fuzzy Semi-Markovian Jump Delay Systems Via Quantized Sampled-Data Control
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: This article, by quantized sampled-data controller (QS-DC), addresses asynchronous control for T-S fuzzy semi-Markovian jump delay systems (TSFSMJDSs), which a weak innitesimal operator (WIO) working on a function with double semi-Markovian jump parameters (DSMJPs). Firstly, an innovative augmented Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional (LKF) is formated that includes both the message of states within the sampled-data intervals and involves with DSMJPs, which not only fully utilize the real sample pattern but also loosen the monotonic constraint of LKF. In addition, the designed QS-DC can enhance the control performance and design flexibility. Finally, verifying the feasibility of theoretical results via a numerical example.

Author Keywords: time-delay T-S fuzzy semi-Markovian jump systems

articleTitle: How the Representation Similarity Between Layers Affects the Random Vector Functional Link Neural Network?
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Random vector functional link neural network (RVFLNN) is a fast learning model for single-hidden layer neural networks. The optimal output weight vector of RVFLNN is determined by the pseudo-inverse of the concatenation of the input matrix and enhancement matrix; however, how the representation similarity of the input layer and enhancement layer affects the random vector functional link neural network is still unknown in the literature. To this end, in this paper, we conduct a comprehensive investigation of the relationship between the input layer and enhancement layer. Moreover, by using the canonical correlation analysis (CCA) to define the statistical similarity of the input layer and the enhancement layer, we propose a pretraining method for RVFLNN. The main idea is to adjust the network weights connecting the input layer and enhancement layer to decrease the similarity between layers using the gradient method. Simulations are conducted on ten UCI classification datasets to verify the effectiveness of the proposed pretraining algorithms.

Author Keywords: Random vector functional link neural network

articleTitle: Zeroth-Order Proximal Stochastic Recursive Momentum Algorithm for Nonconvex Nonsmooth Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a zeroth-order proximal stochastic recursive momentum algorithm(ZO-ProxSTORM) with mini-batch for solving problems where the explicit gradients of the objective function are difficult to calculate or only the objective function values are available. Then, we analyze the convergence of the proposed algorithm under suitable assumptions. Finally, some numerical experiments are given to illustrate the efficiency of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Online Synchronous Iterative Algorithm for Optimal Control of Stochastic Affine Nonlinear Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In this paper, a synchronous iterative algorithm based on reinforcement learning is proposed for solving the optimal control problem of stochastic affine nonlinear systems subject to state-dependent noise. The algorithm solves the related Hamilton-Jacobi equations online, which are nonlinear and difficult to solve directly, especially when higher-order nonlinear systems are involved. The algorithm is constructed based on an actor/critic structure, which permits the critic and actor neural networks (NNs) formed by value function approximation to be updated synchronously. Persistence of excitation is applied to stochastic nonlinear systems. The author presents an implementation of the algorithm and proves that the NN weights converge to the ideal values. A simulation example validates the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Multivariate Time Series Classification Based on Multi-Channel Representation Model and Broad Learning System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Multivariate time series classification is a crucial topic in data mining with far-reaching implications in areas such as finance, healthcare, and industry. In this paper, a novel multivariate time series classification method is proposed. First, a representation model based on local, global, and time-dependent information is constructed. In order to effectively supervise training process of the representation model, an adaptive joint loss function is designed so that the weight of the loss module can be dynamically adjusted. Subsequently, the trained representation model is employed to map original data into a new representation space. In addition, a broad learning system is applied to classify these representations. According to some experimental results on 30 benchmark datasets, the proposed method can achieve better performance in multivariate time series classification tasks.

articleTitle: Adaptive Event-Triggered $H_{\infty}$ Consensus of Leader-Following Multi-Agent Systems Under Hybrid Random Cyber Attacks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> consistency control problem of leader-follower multi-agent systems (MASs) under hybrid random cyber attacks is investigated in this article based on the adaptive event triggering mechanism. For the first time, the exposure of each agent to hybrid random cyber attacks and external disturbances is considered simultaneously, an appropriate adaptive event triggering control protocol is designed. Meanwhile, considering the impact of time lag on system consistency, by converting the leader-following error system into a time-delay error system and using the Lyapunov-Krosovskii functional technique, the sufficient conditions for the system's <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> exponential stability are deduced. Lastly, numerical simulation is used to confirm the control protocol's superiority and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Boosting Few-Shot Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification with Language-Guided Multimodal Prompt Tuning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Remote sensing image Scene classification is an important research topic in remote sensing community and has evoked a growing concern with the recent development of deep learning techniques. However, the requirement of a large amount of annotations brings great challenges to deep learning-based scene classification approaches. Visual-linguistic pretraining models, which improve the transferability of visual models using the supervision information of text, create a new way for the task under label scarcity scenario. In this paper, we explore the novel approach of prompt engineering, aiming to achieve satisfactory performance of multi-modal pretraining models on downstream remote sensing image scene classification task with minimal amounts of training data. Experiments were conducted on multiple publicly available datasets. The results indicate that training the learnable prompts with a small number of samples can yield impressive results, surpassing the few-shot transfer learning results of the best-performing pre-trained models.

articleTitle: Control of Sewage Treatment Based on Optimization and Deep Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In order to enhance the effluent water quality while reducing energy consumption, this paper proposes a multi-objective optimization control algorithm based on IDBO-SENet-BiLSTM-SelfAttention and MOALO. Firstly, an improved DBO algorithm is employed to optimize the hybrid prediction model for predicting energy consumption and effluent water quality. Secondly, the MOALO algorithm is utilized to obtain dynamic optimal setpoints <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{S}_{\mathbf{O},\mathbf{5}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{S}_{\mathbf{NO},\mathbf{2}}$</tex>. Subsequently, a PI controller is employed for setpoint tracking control. Finally, the proposed method is applied to the BSM1 simulation model. The results demonstrate that this approach can dynamically optimize setpoints and achieve tracking control, resulting in significant improvements in both energy consumption and water quality. Moreover, the average values of various effluent water quality indicators meet the emission standards, confirming the effectiveness of this method in the field of wastewater treatment.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Algorithm of Quantum-Behaved Particle Swarm Optimization and Adam for ANN Training and Application for Classification Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: The study of neural networks has become increasingly popular as artificial intelligence has advanced. In addition to several new types of networks and their applications in various fields, neural network optimization has also drawn a lot of attention. Traditional techniques for optimizing the parameters of neural networks are gradient descent algorithms. The drawback of gradient descent algorithms is that they may easily fall into local optima because of the characteristics of local optimization. Meanwhile, several meta-heuristic algorithms have been attempted to optimize neural networks, but the performance is also limited due to insufficient fine search capability. This work proposes the hybrid algorithm HAQPSO to improve the draw-back of gradient descent algorithms, which not only combines Adam with the Quantum-behaved Particle Swarm Optimization (QPSO) but also introduces the hybrid strategy to facilitate information transfer between the algorithms and enhances the efficiency. The proposed algorithm was tested on the Iris dataset and compared with classical gradient descent algorithms and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The experimental results prove that HAQPSO can improve the searching capability while enhancing stability and achieving fast convergence, which is a competitive algorithm.

articleTitle: Environmental Sound Classification Based on Continual Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: With the rapid development of industry, new types of environmental sounds are emerging. Learning and recognizing various sounds is particularly important. However, if neural networks learn new knowledge like humans, they will almost forget the learned knowledge, which is known as the phenomenon of catastrophic forgetting. Continual learning methods based on generative replay could alleviate this problem, but in the face of complex, large datasets, the performance is not ideal. In response, inspired by the interaction between the hippocampus and neocortex, this paper constructs a feature generative replay model for environmental sound classification (FGR-ES). Specifically, during the knowledge learning process, the sound features are extracted using a feature extractor, and then a W-GAN framework is trained with the extracted features to simulate old data. Then, when a new task appears, the encoder is utilized to extract new task features and interact with the generated fake data feature to achieve the fusion of new and old task information. Finally, this information is employed to update the classifier and realize the environmental sound classification. Besides, experimental results on ESC10, ESC50, and Urbansound8K show that the proposed method achieves competitive results.

articleTitle: Novel Automatic Clustering Algorithm Based on Proximity Graphs for DNA Microarray Data
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: DNA microarray (gene microarray or DNA chip) can provide a vast resource of medical diagnostic and disease understanding. The clustering of DNA microarray data has become more and more important in the filed of data mining. Sometimes, the understanding of the correct behavior of genes is hard because of the large amount of data. Especially the research on high-dimensional data cluster boundary detection has not yet entered a mature stage. To obtain better clustering results and clear cluster boundary, we proposed a genetic clustering algorithm based on the shortest path, referred to as NAP3M (Novel Automatic Multi-step Maxmin and Merging algorithm based on Proximity-graphs) clustering algorithm. The experimental result shows that our NAP3M is effective and promising.

articleTitle: Estimation of Concrete Compressive Strength: A Neural Ordinary Differential Equation Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: The 28-day concrete compressive strength(CCS) is one of the most significant indicators required by the construction industry. The existing methods require making concrete samples and conducting compressive strength tests through physical experiments in the sample age of 28 days. Waiting time of the experiments increases the cost in time and financial, which can not meet the actual demand. The advent of computational intelligence makes it possible to estimate the CCS. Many scholars use regression models to estimate the CCS. However, the formation of concrete strength is a complex dynamic system. The use of regression models can place limitations on estimates, limiting the potential for effects. It is inappropriate to simplify a complex dynamic system as a regression problem. Differential equations are widely used to describe dynamical systems. Neural ordinary differential equations draw on the idea of differential equations. But unlike ordinary differential equations in mathematics, the derivative functions of ordinary differential equations are modeled by neural networks. We proposed a novel approach to model the dynamical system of concrete. Furthermore, it provides a novel approach to estimating the 28-day CCS by modeling concrete dynamic systems based on Neural ODE. The experimental results show our approach achieves acceptable accuracy.

articleTitle: MIMRD: An Enhanced Masked Image Modeling Reverse Distillation for Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Anomaly detection is a meaningful and important research topic. Currently, unsupervised methods for anomaly detection demonstrate exceptional performance. Reverse distillation (RD) is an effective approach that ensures minimal latency while demonstrating overly strong generalization ability, causing abnormal features to be generalized as normal features in anomaly detection tasks. However, there may be instances where the model's generalization ability becomes overly dominant. To address this problem, we propose an enhanced masked image modeling reverse distillation (MIMRD). In this paper, we establish a state-of-the-art benchmark on the challenging MVTec dataset for both identifying and localizing anomalies. This model reconstructs the features with pseudo anomalies and enhance the difference in anomalousness through utilization of projection layer. Then, the student model regresses to the normal features generated by the teacher model. From the experimental results, our method has achieved competitive results without a significant increase in inference time.

articleTitle: Virtual Model Interaction Based on Single RGB Camera
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Nowadays, gesture recognition has been sufficiently developed and used in many areas, for example, you can control the model by your gesture, which can provide the audience with a more intuitive understanding of the displayed model and make it easier for the operator to present. However, most methods are based on specific device such as depth sensor, which contributes to gesture recognition cannot be extensively implemented, using a normal RGB camera to track the hand and recognize the gesture becomes a significant issue. Lightweight is also a problem, real-time hand detection and tracking is feasible due to the low level of lightweight. Under the circumstance, cost saving of gesture recognition is a significant issue to exploit. We present a new method using a real-time on-device hand tracking solution to control virtual models in Unreal Engine. We have introduced OneEuro Filter to handle the jitter that occurs when the hand is in motion, affecting the control of the model.

articleTitle: Neuro-Adaptive Time-Varying Formation Control with Collision Avoidance for Nonlinear Multiagent Systems with Unknown Control Directions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Aiming at the nonlinear multiagent systems with unknown control directions, the time-varying formation control problem with obstacle avoidance is studied. Multiple coupled Nussbaum functions are constructed to deal with the unknown conrol directions of nonlinear multiagent systems. Combining artificial potential function with dynamic surface control technology, a novel neuro-adaptive control method is proposed to realize time-varying formation, which can effectively avoid obstacles encountered without collision between agent individuals. The bounded stability of the closed-loop system is proved by Lyapunov stability theory, and the formation tracking error converges to a small neighborhood of zero. Finally, simulation results are given to verify the effectiveness of the proposed time-varying formation control method for the nonlinear multiagent systems with unknown control directions.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network Based Algorithm for Intrusion Detection in Internet of Things Databases
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is generally isolated from external networks using firewall technology[1]. However, with the continuous development of IoT technology, the interconnection is becoming closer and the frequency of intrusions is increasing[2]. This poses greater challenges for security measures. Therefore, it is crucial to efficiently detect intrusions in the IoT. This article proposes a convolutional neural network-based algorithm for intrusion detection in IoT databases[3]. IoT data has fixed formats, real-time characteristics, and short fields. Therefore, training with a convolutional neural network improves efficiency[4]. The algorithm monitors and analyzes network traffic in the IoT system, uses a convolutional neural network to classify and determine traffic data[5], and thus achieves attack detection in the IoT system. The algorithm designed in this article achieves an accuracy rate of 99.4%, which not only improves the accuracy of intrusion detection compared to SVM and KNN algorithms but also reduces false positive rates.

articleTitle: Research on Location Method of Mine Micro-Seismic Source Based on Inter Quartile Range and Newton-Raphson Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In order to improve the accuracy of microseismic localization, avoid the error concentration phenomenon in the inversion model of the optimization class algorithm, and improve the robustness of microseismic source localization, a microseismic source localization method based on robust analysis is proposed. The four-four combination localization model is established, and the approximate solution results of the seismic source are obtained by solving with Newton iteration method; the IQR robust value determination criterion and three-component weighted center of gravity method are introduced to gradually eliminate the outliers of class I and class II in the preliminary results, and finally the final seismic source optimization results are obtained according to the IQR triple-mean value method. Through the blasting data test of a mine, the three-component positioning errors of the optimized seismic source are 2.70 m, 0.54 m and 6.80 m, and the absolute spatial distance is 7.34 m.
